vowel_sequence.note: Assumes reading: "when you see a vowel in a Spanish word". Suggest: "From now on, every vowel you hear in a Spanish word is one of these five."

concept_tion_intro.note: Assumes reading: "The accent mark on the ó tells you where to stress the word. That's all it does." A listener never sees the ó. Suggest: "The stress always lands on that ending: -ción."

worked_nation.note: Assumes reading: "The stress falls on the ó. That's what the accent mark is telling you." Suggest: "The stress falls on the end: nación."

concept_al_intro.note: Spelling-based: "you don't change a single letter", "spelled exactly the same", "Identical spelling", "no accent mark is needed". Suggest "it's the same word in Spanish" and ending the last paragraph at "the stress always pulls to that final AL."

worked_normal.note: Spelling-based: "n-o-r-m-a-l in both languages. Not one letter changes." Suggest: "normal is the same word in both languages."

worked_natural.note: Spelling-based: "same spelling again". Suggest: "the same word again".

concept_silent_h.note: Assumes reading: "It gets written, but it is never pronounced" and "when you see an H at the start of a Spanish word". A listener only ever hears the vowel. Suggest closing with: "So when an English word starts with H, like hospital, the Spanish version starts straight on the vowel."

worked_electric.note: Assumes reading: "The accent on the é tells you". Also the arrow: "electric" → add "-o" will be spoken "electric becomes add o". Suggest: "electric: add an o to the end, and you get eléctrico. The stress falls on the second syllable: eléctrico."

worked_querer.note: Spelling-based: "a small spelling change in the middle". Suggest: "a small sound change in the middle".
